extracted.intended_audience: researchers, hiring/tenure/promotion committees, and university research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting responsible research assessment at an institutional level in line with the San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA), covering hiring, promotion, funding decisions, and how to use metrics and qualitative evidence. Aims to shift evaluation from journal-based metrics to content- and impact-focused judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use journal-based metrics as surrogates for quality
rubrics_metrics.description: DORA’s key tenet is to “not use journal-based metrics, such as Journal Impact Factors (JIFs), as surrogate measures of the quality of individual research articles, to assess an individual scientist’s contributions, or in hiring, promotion, or funding decisions”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition on relying on journal-level metrics (e.g., JIF) to judge individual articles or researchers; instead assess the content and contribution of the specific research output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use peer review and expert judgement as central to assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The University is committed to the critical role that peer review and expert judgement plays in the assessment of research, but also recognises the value that quantitative metrics can play in complementing and supporting decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise expert qualitative assessment while allowing quantitative metrics only to complement and support, not replace, judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about criteria for hiring, tenure and promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about the criteria used to reach hiring, tenure, and promotion decisions, clearly highlighting, especially for early-stage investigators, that the scientific content of a paper is much more important than publication metrics or the identity of the journal in which it was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and communicate the decision criteria used by committees; emphasise content-based evaluation and make special accommodations/clarity for early-stage investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider all research outputs and a broad range of impact measures
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of research assessment, consider the value and impact of all research outputs (including datasets and software) in addition to research publications, and consider a broad range of impact measures including qualitative indicators of research impact, such as influence on policy and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expand the unit of assessment beyond traditional publications to include datasets, software, and other outputs; include qualitative impact evidence (e.g., policy influence, practice change) alongside quantitative indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess on scientific content rather than publication metrics (committee members)
rubrics_metrics.description: When involved in committees making decisions about funding, hiring, tenure, or promotion, make assessments based on scientific content rather than publication metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee members should prioritise evaluation of the work's scientific merit, rigor, originality and contribution rather than relying on journal prestige or numeric journal metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite primary literature to give appropriate credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever appropriate, cite primary literature in which observations are first reported rather than reviews in order to give credit where credit is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage citation practices that attribute priority and credit to original reports; avoid over-relying on secondary/review articles when primary sources exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a range of article-level metrics and indicators on statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a range of article metrics and indicators on personal/supporting statements, as evidence of the impact of individual published articles and other research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and evaluators may present and consider multiple article-level indicators (downloads, citations, altmetrics, usage) as part of supporting evidence for impact, rather than a single journal metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge inappropriate reliance on Journal Impact Factors and teach best practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge research assessment practices that rely inappropriately on Journal Impact Factors and promote and teach best practice that focuses on the value and influence of specific research outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actively question and change institutional and community norms that use JIFs inappropriately; engage in training and advocacy to shift assessment culture toward output-level value and influence.
